fit.b2b_caveat: A back-to-back is only flagged when the previous day's game is present in the captured results. Results now run from 2026-11-06, so back-to-backs running into 2026-11-09 and later are fully detected; back-to-backs running into 2026-11-06 itself are not.

strategies.name: Side edge vs reference
strategies.rule: Play the side when the originated margin differs from the reference spread by at least 3.0 points.
strategies.why: The additive efficiency model collapses to a net-rating difference, so a side edge can only come from shrinkage, home court, rest and availability. A 3.0-point filter keeps only the plays where those refinements actually bite.

strategies.name: Total edge vs reference
strategies.rule: Play over/under when the originated total differs from the reference total by at least 6.0 points.
strategies.why: The reference total is simply the two teams' published scoring averages added together, so it ignores defence entirely. The gap is the opponent-adjustment signal.

strategies.name: Moneyline value
strategies.rule: Play the moneyline when the originated win probability differs from the reference win probability by at least 6 percentage points and the originated price is shorter than +200.
strategies.why: Moneylines punish favourites less than spreads do, so a large probability gap is the efficient way to monetise a side edge on a big favourite.

strategies.name: Pace-driven total
strategies.rule: Totals only, and only when the game's expected pace is at least 3.0 possessions per 48 minutes away from the league average AND the total edge is at least 4.0 points.
strategies.why: Pace is the most persistent team stat in the official advanced table. Restricting totals to genuine pace outliers removes the games where the total edge is just defensive noise.

strategies.name: Back-to-back fade
strategies.rule: Exactly one team is on the second night of a back-to-back and the originated margin differs from the reference spread by at least 2.0 points.
strategies.why: Rest is the one schedule effect that is fully observable from the official schedule and results. Both teams are held to the same threshold so the filter is not simply 'fade the tired team'.

strategies.name: Two-leg cross-game parlay
strategies.rule: Take the two highest-edge S1/S2 legs of the day from DIFFERENT games, each with an edge at least 2.5, and parlay them.
strategies.why: Legs from different games are independent, so the parlay price is the product of the legs and the only edge is the model edge on each leg.

strategies.name: Same-game parlay (side + total)
strategies.rule: In the same game, parlay the side leg and the total leg when each has an edge of at least 2.5 and the modelled side/total correlation is at most 0.30.
strategies.why: Same-game legs share possessions, so they are correlated. Pricing them as independent is the classic SGP error; the copula price is published next to the independent price so the difference is visible.

gate_definitions.name: Sample size
gate_definitions.definition: At least 30 graded plays; 10-29 is provisional.

gate_definitions.name: Calibration
gate_definitions.definition: Observed hit rate within 8 pp of the mean predicted probability.

gate_definitions.name: Edge over break-even
gate_definitions.definition: Mean modelled probability at or above 52.38% (break-even at -110).

gate_definitions.name: Skill, not luck
gate_definitions.definition: Wilson 95% lower bound on the hit rate above 52.38%; exact binomial p reported.

gate_definitions.name: Stability
gate_definitions.definition: Bootstrap 95% CI of the model's margin MAE sits entirely below the reference model's MAE.

gate_definitions.name: Availability robustness
gate_definitions.definition: A play must survive flipping every Questionable player to Out (needs the official report for the graded window).
